newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten to cooperate with leader-in-waiting.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten to cooperate with leader-in-waiting.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Wednesday reaffirmed his opposition to an interim legislature China will install here next year but said it would not affect his willingness to cooperate with the territory's next leader.

"You know perfectly well what (our) position is as regards the provisional legislature...and I don't think anybody is expecting us to change it," Patten told reporters after a public function on Wednesday.
"(But) it certainly won't affect the willingness on our part to provide all reasonable co-operation to Mr Tung," he said.

Shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa was chosen under careful Chinese supervision last week by a 400-member panel to become Hong Kong's first chief executive when the colony reverts to China after more than 150 years of British rule next July 1.
But the territory of 6.3 million is jittery about China's intended move to replace the elected legislative council at the handover with the provisional chamber, due to be formed on Saturday.
Patten has said he regards the provisional legislature as unjustifiable and reprehensible and has ruled out cooperation with it.
Tung, who was anointed as Hong Kong's first post-handover leader by Chinese leaders in Beijing's Great Hall of the People on Wednesday, had agreed to meet Patten soon, the governor said.
"We have agreed that we should meet after his visit to Peking (Beijing) and after all the formalities of his appointment are out of the way," Patten said.
"He confirmed that in a letter to me the other day."
